messages:
cs_amy: heads-up — AcmeCorp reporting a sudden spike of 503s around 2026-03-18 11:22 UTC. Customer pasted errors: "500 Internal Server Error" and "upstream inference worker crashed". Provided request IDs req_abc123, req_def456. They reported a very large context ( ~65k tokens ) and sustained QPS ~120 on a single hosted model.
eng-oncall: ack. I'm attaching to this thread, digging into logs now. Do we have the exact request payload from CS ticket?
cs_amy: pasted payload + request IDs into the support ticket thread. Customer also said it started after a long prompt + file upload. They want ETA.
eng-oncall: quick findings: runner on host gpu-3 (hosted-prod-7) restarted repeatedly. Kernel log shows GPU OOM followed by segfault. sample from runner stderr:
```
[2026-03-18T11:22:41Z] ERROR infer-runner: CUDA error: out of memory
[2026-03-18T11:22:41Z] ERROR infer-runner: Caught SIGSEGV at 0x7fffa2b3
stack: 0x400d21 0x4012ab 0x7fb1c2...
```
infra_sre: confirming — container id `c5102` on node `hosted-prod-7-gpu-3` crashed and was restarted by kubelet 3x in ~2m. I’ve pulled `dmesg` and NVML logs, looks like a memory surge then process abort. Temporarily cordoned the node and launched a new replacement instance to avoid collateral impact.
infra_sre: immediate mitigation applied: removed Acme route from pool `gpu-pool-a` and added to `fallback-cpu-pool` via routing API. Waiting to see if customer traffic stabilizes.
eng-oncall: thanks. Two-prong plan: 1) keep routing to fallback pool for now; 2) collect coredump + full runner logs for postmortem. Commands I ran to collect artifacts:
```
sudo journalctl -u infer-runner -o short-iso > /tmp/infer-runner-gpu3.log
sudo coredumpctl dump CONTAINER_ID=c5102 --output=/tmp/c5102.core
kubectl logs -n hosted deploy/infer-runner -c runner --since=10m > /tmp/kube-runner.log
```
james: suggested short-term customer-facing mitigations: reduce their max_context to 32k for now, or route to `model-quantized-v2` (lower memory profile). In Console: Projects > AcmeCorp > Routing > add rule with priority 10 -> route to `fallback-cpu-pool` or `model-quantized-v2`. Also add a reject guardrail to return 4xx for requests with context >128k to avoid letting the runtime crash.
cs_amy: customer asked for concrete next steps they can try now. Can we give a short list I can paste?
eng-oncall: paste this for them: 1) retry with `model-quantized-v2` (lower memory) 2) trim attachments or send as smaller chunks <32k tokens 3) we routed you to fallback pool — if you still see 5xx provide the request IDs.
elinor: drafting message to Acme:
"Hi — we're sorry for the disruption. We've routed your requests to a fallback pool to restore traffic while we investigate. Please try the quantized model or reduce prompt size to ~32k tokens. We'll follow up within 45 minutes with root cause and a remediation plan. — Elinor, Redwood Support"
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-00057 (severity=P1) — runbook: /runbooks/hosted-503s
eng-oncall: reproduction notes for ENG (internal): to reproduce locally use the harness with a synthetic large-context payload:
```
# from infra/diagnostics
ENV=staging ./heavy_context_test.sh --model main-v1 --tokens 65000 --qps 100 --duration 60
```
james: follow-ups for engineering: 1) add a guard in the routing layer to fail-fast on >128k context, 2) add a soft memory cap per-request + graceful 5xx->4xx conversion, 3) investigate why KV-prefetch and dynamic batching combined with large context produce an OOM instead of a clean error.
infra_sre: full logs uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/7321112222/ — including coredump, nvml logs, and `journalctl` output.
cs_amy: customer escalation: Acme replied they're seeing reduced errors after fallback routing, but they want ETA on permanent fix and a timeline for avoiding this recurring.
eng-oncall: current ETA: 30-45m to finish debug and push routing guard. If we confirm a code fix is required, timeline will be longer; postmortem will include timeline. We'll update every 15 minutes.
elinor: sending the drafted message now, cc: customer success and legal.
eng-oncall: incident acknowledged and assigned to eng-runtime for root cause analysis. Creating postmortem placeholder in /incidents/7321112222.
cs_amy: thanks everyone — I’ll update Acme with the message and forward any new request IDs.
eng-oncall: keeping this thread live. Last note: do not re-enable KV-prefetch on that node until we confirm memory behavior.
